domains.title: Pattern editing, algorithms, channel ranges and storage axes
domains.interaction_strategy: Pairwise pattern, step, algorithm, active state and range; named preview/paint/cancel triples; three retained deterministic seeds drive 4,800 ordered edits through the real sequencer control with full-state checks and cross-identity isolation probes.
residual_gaps: Generated control sequences cover two boundary songs, all 16 patterns, all 16 channels and all 64 steps, crossing tap, wrapped/equal length, long-reset and accepted/rejected range operations. The unbounded sequence space remains represented by three fixed seeds rather than exhaustively enumerated.
The page integration matrix covers every output position at each algorithm boundary; exhaustive all-fader products remain delegated to independently-oracled drum_ops arithmetic tests.

domains.title: Grid, screen, navigation and gesture state
domains.interaction_strategy: State transitions and pairwise held-key, page, encoder and release-order combinations.
residual_gaps: The semantic page-object layer is explicitly deferred. Existing native cases remain the refactor oracle for visible page state.

The real m_grid/press unit path proves held-state cleanup and a clean first tap through grid.add reconnect. M-GRID-001 characterizes the native emulator lifecycle in both lanes and repeated controlled runs: grid_connection synthesizes held-key releases before g.remove, committing a valid range. It therefore cannot validate the physical no-release disconnect semantics decided for S29.

domains.title: Device configuration, patch recall and value domains
domains.interaction_strategy: Exhaust codecs and slots; pairwise device, sentinel, port, channel, recall and reassignment.
residual_gaps: S3 EX Braids slot semantics remain blocked by an unavailable EX profile and no manual oracle. Current merged-index behavior is unit-characterized; EX Braids indexing is excluded from refactors until a profile-level oracle exists.

All ten assignment slots cross initial assignment, identical reassignment, CC-to-NRPN replacement, clear, repeated clear, callback retirement and copy isolation on channel 16; all ten definitions, locks and slides round-trip independently on song 96/channel 16. Native cases remain the user-visible assignment oracles.

domains.title: Masks, trig parameters, probability, trigless and locks
domains.interaction_strategy: Exhaustive 0-100 probability draws and all ten lock/slide slots, crossed with boundary song, channel and step identities; deterministic pairwise native cases retain trigless-slide-clock and persistence interactions.
residual_gaps: All ten slots and boundary song/channel/step identities are unit-covered. One same-step history guard crosses partial undo, serialization/reload, redo, branch replacement and undo-all across all ten slots. MIDI reassignment lifecycle is composed in H03 and native M-PARAM/M-PATCH cases; norns-family ownership is anchored by M-XA-005/006; stock lock arithmetic is covered by step matrices.

Probability is exhaustive over 0..100 against draws 0..99. Locks, random offsets, song transitions and persistence are retained as deterministic pairwise/triple native interactions rather than their unbounded Cartesian product.

domains.title: Pattern and scale merging arithmetic

finite_axes.name: numeric merge modes
finite_axes.coverage: up, down and average partitions plus all 16 priority identities

domains.interaction_strategy: Literal formula matrices cover negative values, half-up ties and fractional lengths; exhaustive source cardinality and priority identity sweeps are combined with order, immutability, result-copy and channel-isolation invariants.
residual_gaps: User-visible MIDI-bound consequences of out-of-range merged values remain owned by native behaviour cases.

Working-pattern recomposition covers source edits, unassignment, reassignment and song-copy isolation. Merge-to-MIDI guards cover duplicate equal sources, the documented lower-tie rule, configured root plus transpose and all ten named pentatonic selections. The full Cartesian product of all sixteen source contents remains partitioned by independently-oracled arithmetic matrices.

domains.title: Scales, quantisation and pitch composition

finite_axes.name: production scale types
finite_axes.coverage: exhaustive arithmetic, number and name binding

finite_axes.name: composition stages
finite_axes.coverage: root, degree, rotation, transpose, octave, mask, quantise

domains.interaction_strategy: Exhaust finite scale slots, scale types, MIDI pitches and all eight pentatonic switches; pairwise pitch stages plus explicit merged-note/random-offset switch contexts and song-copy cache isolation.
residual_gaps: Save across song intentionally links one scale table across existing song slots (user decision S35, 2026-09-11); warm-cache invalidation and linked rotation are covered on songs 1, 48 and 96.

Direct in-place mutation outside supported save/rotation routes is characterised by quantiser unit tests and is not a documented product workflow; production UI saves remain anchored by M-SCALE-CACHE-001. Merge-to-MIDI integration now covers all ten documented pentatonic selections plus root/transpose/lower-tie composition.

domains.title: Chord voices, strum, arp, spread and acceleration
domains.interaction_strategy: Exhaust voice/order/mute and velocity axes; partition timing magnitudes; pairwise modifiers plus maximum five-voice overlap, repeated-pitch ownership, Stop and probability-rejection lifecycle triples.
residual_gaps: Delayed strum output ownership is pinned: pitch uses the scale active at the delayed onset while the parent chord's MIDI device owns note-on and release; native M-ARP-012/013 cover applied live-scale edits during a running arp.

Maximum-overlap release ownership is unit-covered; representative native timing remains linked to existing chord/arp behaviour cases rather than multiplying the complete 259-case chord-shape matrix by every timing magnitude.

domains.title: Internal timing, divisions, slides, swing and shuffle
domains.interaction_strategy: Exact pulse matrices; pairwise division, feel, length and reset; named slide lifecycle triples.
residual_gaps: Severe delayed external callback responsiveness is covered by M-SYNC-023 and a coroutine unit: Stop preempts stale catch-up after a one-second Lua stall.
Slide replacement, clear, wrap, reset, retiming, capacity and all ten slots are covered; the unbounded product of every clock rate, shuffle and slide combination remains partitioned.

domains.title: External MIDI clock, transport and synchronization

finite_axes.name: fault classes
finite_axes.coverage: missing, extra, jitter, drift, step, burst

domains.interaction_strategy: Exact controlled pulse ordinals plus real-time bounds and deterministic fault/lifecycle sequences.
residual_gaps: M-SYNC-006 remains a recorded later-refactor 10 ms phase defect; its threshold is unchanged.
Runtime overload is a bounded Lua event-thread stall, not physical-norns performance equivalence.

domains.title: Live note and parameter recording
domains.interaction_strategy: First press to final release state transitions; pairwise source/channel/arm/page and named song-lock-clock triples.
residual_gaps: All ten live parameter-recording slots update together through the composed clock path, remain channel-isolated, and retire at the pattern wrap; all ten definitions, locks and slides independently round-trip at song 96/channel 16.
Live ten-slot edits with modulation, song transitions and persistence are partitioned across native M-REC-PARAM and M-TRIPLE interactions rather than exhaustively multiplied in Lua.

Keyboard input-channel semantics are resolved: M-MIDI-002 covers all 16 input channels on two ports and both release forms; M-REC-016 and M-REC-024/025 prove selected-Mosaic-channel recording and overlapping-source ownership.

domains.title: Memory, undo, redo and bounded history
domains.interaction_strategy: Deterministic generated edits with retained seeds plus branch, truncation, wrap and persistence partitions.
residual_gaps: S58 is fixed with M-MEMORY-014 at the production 5000-action bound plus minimized undo, undo-all, interleaved-key, serialization, legacy-history and corruption-recovery units.

The two production event types cross all mask fields, four chord voices, ten lock slots, boundary songs/steps, undo, redo-all, branch truncation and memory serialization; full project save/reload remains behavior-owned by M-MEMORY-006 and combined persistence cases.

domains.title: Song state, persistence, validation, autosave and migration
domains.interaction_strategy: Round trips, malformed partitions, every IO stage, lifecycle cleanup and immutable fixtures.
residual_gaps: Saving is not transactional: a failed write may leave a partial target. Later load rejects unreadable partial data without replacing live state or resuming autosave; automatic reconstruction is not a supported contract.
Frozen current and 1.2.12 projects pass the pinned tabutil/validation/migration path. Add another immutable fixture when a materially distinct schema ships.

residual_gaps: The Digitakt 2 legacy-half exception is confined to NRPN fields by the all-device default-assignment matrix; CC assignments and every other device retain standard or nil mode.

domains.title: Performance, recovery and composition workflows

finite_axes.name: completed dense workloads
finite_axes.coverage: PERF-002, PERF-003, PERF-004 and executable PERF-008

domains.interaction_strategy: Performance ownership is R01 and the performance ledger. Retain the existing fast Lua regression only; do not add unit/integration performance matrices here.
residual_gaps: A deterministic 1,280-admission slide workload crosses the 1,024-entry ring and verifies every final channel/slot owner under a 5 ms host characterisation bound; it passed three integrated repeats. This is not physical-norns equivalence.
PERF-003 16-channel timing fails 2/3 repeats.

Controlled M-ENDURANCE-001 passed three fresh-process 608.29-second logical runs with exact event counts and 1 ns logical error. The real-time ten-minute run failed after a persistent 42–43 ms port-1 phase shift began around 126 seconds (p99 43.336 ms, final 42.392 ms). This remains a real-time musical-timing failure and refactor blocker. The retained run has no native clock trace, so direct cause is unproven; generic trace evidence from emulator commit `2223a23` shows the pinned official internal-clock skip-ahead branch can produce an exact 41.6666666667 ms displacement after a two-deadline miss. It neither attributes this endurance shift to that branch nor establishes physical-norns behaviour.

PERF-004 has an executable constrained input-pressure recipe. PERF-008 now has an executable 16-channel overload/recovery recipe with exact MIDI ownership and timeline fingerprints, post-overload grid/frame oracles, CFS-throttling proof and the unchanged 10/50/20 ms timing gates. Its clean-revision diagnostic retained at /home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-runs/perf-overload-recovery-20260912-07 failed p99/maximum/final phase at about 70/70/68 ms while ownership, rendering, service, memory and queue-recovery gates passed. This is a refactor blocker, not a hardware claim. PERF-005 through PERF-007 still need individual executable recipes after duplicate-coverage reconciliation.
Final full suite waits for held UX verdicts.
